name: Fergus mac Léti

attributes.attribute: a water monster in Lough Rudraige
died with his head facing backward

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fergus mac Léti was a king of Ulster. His adventures may have inspired Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels. While sailing he met small water sprites. The sprites tried to rob him and drown him. He overpowered them and held them captives. They granted him three wishes. He wished to swim underwater in ponds, lakes, and the ocean. The fairies added one condition. He could not submerge himself in Lough Rudraige in Ulster. He swam there anyway and met the muirdris, a fearsome water monster. The monster so terrified him that his head turned backward. His druids ruled that a backward head was not a blemish. They covered all the mirrors at Emain Macha. For seven years he lived without knowing of his change. A woman he had mistreated told him the truth. He returned to Lough Rudraige and killed the muirdris. He fell dead of exhaustion, his head still facing backward.

okr.objective: Fergus mac Léti is an Ulster king whose fight with the water monster muirdris ended with his death.
key_results: Fergus mac Léti was a king of Ulster.
He received three wishes from water sprites he had overpowered.
